description:
FILED s470bk (Opus, 2026-09-05) while shipping #1057, and MEASURED both
before and after it (scratch/s470bk/p1057/alias.pl row 05).  PRE-EXISTING.

    my $n = 0; sub k { $n++; return "kk" }
    my %m; $m{a} = "z"; $m{k()} .= "q"; print $n;
        perl 1      PCL 2        <- the side effect runs twice

THE CAUSE.  `%store-back-form` (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp) builds a compound
assignment over an accessor place as

    (setf PLACE (op PLACE VALUE))

so the SYNTACTIC place appears twice and its subforms are evaluated twice.
For a boxed scalar place the same function already binds the place to a temp
once ("PLACE is evaluated once"), and #1057 made the NESTED element place bind
its container and key to temps too â so today the flat element place is the
only member of the family that still double-evaluates, and one program can
give two answers (`$h{a}{k()} .= 1` calls k() once, `$h{k()} .= 1` twice).

THE FIX IS ONE PREDICATE: `%p-nested-elem-place-p` becomes "any element
place" (p-gethash / p-aref, container walked by `expand-autoviv`, which is the
IDENTITY on a non-chain container) â the temps then bind for every element
compound assign and the double evaluation is gone family-wide.  It was
deliberately NOT done in #1057's commit because it changes the emitted shape
of a very common hot operation (`$h{k} .= â¦`), and an agent brief that does
not run the full sweep cannot validate that breadth; the narrow condition
could be proved by the gate alone.

BAR when taken: the probe above and its `$a[f()] .= â¦` twin, a bench read of
a hash-element compound-assign loop before and after (two lexical bindings
that are immediately consumed should be free â measure it, do not assume),
the gate, and the full sweep (a `cl/` change).

=== DONE (s473b) ===
FIXED s473b (Opus, 2026-09-07), commit d8ef2a42 â the ONE PREDICATE this task
proposed: `%p-nested-elem-place-p` became `%p-elem-place-p` ("is this an
element place"), so `%store-back-form`'s temps bind for every element compound
assign and the container/key are evaluated ONCE.  The container still goes
through the chain walker, which is the IDENTITY on a non-chain container, so
#1057's vivification is unchanged.
The SHORT-CIRCUIT assigns were in the same family and were not named in this
task: `p-and-assign` / `p-or-assign` / `p-//=` handed the SYNTACTIC place to
`p-setf` after reading it, and the comment above them called the double
evaluation "harmless for the variable/constant subscripts that occur in
practice" â it was not (`$h{k()} ||= 7` called k() twice, probed).  They share
the seam now (`%p-elem-place-form`).
Probes vs perl 5.40.3 (scratch/s473b/probe/m1152.pl, 13 shapes): identical in
12, default and PCL_OPT=none.  The remaining one is the DEREF spelling
`$r->{k()} .= "z"` â filed as #1351.
BENCH â the bar this task set, and note the INSTRUMENT: `bench-emission-ab.pl`
is the WRONG one for a macro-only change (it builds ONE core from this tree's
runtime and times two EMISSIONS, which are byte-identical here).  A runtime
A/B is needed: one emission, TWO cores, four series interleaved, best-of-7
(scratch/s473b/bench-rt-ab.pl).  Measured on an idle box (load 1.9):
    elemcompound  ($h{a} .= "x"; $a[$i] += 2)   +0.55 %
    elemorassign  ($h{$k} ||= â¦; $h{$k} //= â¦)  -0.43 %
    arrhash       CONTROL (expansion identical) +0.05 %
    cfor          CONTROL                       +0.16 %
The first run read -3 % / -8.7 % on the CONTROLS because N left only ~30 ms of
exec after the subtraction â raise N until the row is seconds, then read it.
Guard: Pl/t/autoviv-02.t row 13, inverse-verified on the 782bc37e extraction.
subject: A compound assign to a FLAT element evaluates its container and KEY twice (`$h{k()} .= "q"` calls k() twice; perl once) â #1057 fixed only the nested spelling
